name: monster

attributes.attribute: a folkloric figure whose gods often were gods of an earlier people
an old deity that became small and appealing in Irish folklore
a monstrous female figure read as a derogatory account of an early deity
monstrosity shows divinity only when joined with shape-shifting or magic powers

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: monster is a folkloric figure in Celtic tradition. The monsters of one people were often the gods of an earlier people. In many Celtic lands the old deities did not grow monstrously large and frightening. Instead they became smaller and appealing, like the Leprechauns and fairies of Irish and Scottish folklore. Giants also appear, chiefly in Britain. Behind their awful faces hide elder gods. Followers of male-centered monotheism often vilified goddesses. Some monstrous female figures, such as the Cailleach, are derogatory accounts of powerful early deities. Monstrosity by itself does not show divinity. It must combine with shape-shifting or other magic powers.
